title: Functions and Return Values
goal: Declare functions with explicit types and implicit return expressions.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Morning: Control Flow Basics

sections.text: Functions in Rust are declared with the `fn` keyword.
Parameters require explicit type annotations, and the return type follows an arrow `->`.

sections.caption: Parameters specify types after a colon.

sections.text: The last expression in a function body becomes its return value. Omit the semicolon to return that value.
Use an explicit `return` keyword for early exits from a function.

sections.caption: Early exit uses return. Final result omits return.

sections.text: When a function returns nothing, it returns the unit type `()`. Omitting `->` implies `-> ()`.
Generic parameters on functions are covered in the Generics deck later.

explanation: Declare functions with explicit types and implicit return expressions.
